blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — aprepitant indication for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting prevention
stem: A client receiving highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy is prescribed aprepitant as part of a multidrug antiemetic regimen. What is the purpose of aprepitant in this setting?

options.A: It is an NK1-receptor antagonist used with other antiemetics to prevent acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting before those symptoms become established.
options.B: It is primarily used after chemotherapy-related nausea and vomiting are already established, because treatment of active symptoms is its labeled role rather than prevention.
options.C: It is a hematopoietic growth factor used to prevent febrile neutropenia by stimulating neutrophil production during highly emetogenic chemotherapy courses.
options.D: It is a mucosal-protective medication used to prevent chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis rather than to prevent acute or delayed nausea and vomiting.

rationale: Current aprepitant labeling identifies aprepitant as a substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist. In combination with other antiemetic agents, it is indicated for prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with highly emetogenic chemotherapy and for prevention of nausea and vomiting with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy. The label states that aprepitant has not been studied for treatment of established nausea and vomiting. Therefore A is correct. B reverses the labeled preventive role, C describes a granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, and D describes a different supportive-care construct.
educational_objective: Recognize aprepitant as an NK1 receptor antagonist used with other antiemetics to prevent acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting rather than to treat established symptoms.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label dated June 11, 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Indications and Usage §1.1 Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Nausea and Vomiting: in combination with other antiemetics, prevention of acute and delayed CINV with highly emetogenic chemotherapy and prevention with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy; §1.3 Limitations of Use: not studied for treatment of established nausea and vomiting.
source_claim_supported: Aprepitant is an NK1 receptor antagonist used with other antiemetics to prevent acute and delayed CINV in specified chemotherapy settings and has not been studied for treatment of established nausea and vomiting.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: identify indications for medications and monitor/evaluate client response to medication therapy.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as substantive supportive-care medication roles without absolute-word distractor cues.
Balanced option length and preserved the label's prevention-versus-established-treatment distinction.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current June 2026 aprepitant indication and limitation. B incorrectly makes it treatment for established symptoms, C and D test other supportive-care mechanisms, and no second defensible answer remains.
